$comment: P6-05 (ADR-155): every place Daisy's code (comments aside) still uses the project's old name, and why. Read by tests/no-harbor-names.test.ts: an occurrence no entry covers fails, and so does an entry that covers nothing. `files` is a glob (or a list), `re` a regular expression matched against the code of one line; an occurrence counts as covered when a match spans it. Keep entries narrow: a new use needs a reason old data, old sessions or old installs give.

entries.why: the injection mark: still written as it is (an external boot core matches it, D-43); readers accept it and 「Daisy 注入」 (ADR-154)
the guard itself: the name it looks for and its self-test samples
a snapshot of what the model was told at an old commit: stored data from before the rename, compared as it was
old environment variable names: HARBOR_X is still read (with a warning) when DAISY_X is not set, and never passed on to commands (ADR-153)
the web build's old sub-path variable, still read with a warning (ADR-153)
the old data directory variable: ignored with a warning (P1-04), so it is named to warn about it and to keep it out of the default
the tests of the renamed environment variables, paths, worktrees and browser storage keys: the old names must still work (ADR-153)
start settings: an old HARBOR_<ID>_BIN still wins over runner.json (ADR-153, ADR-156); the test clears both spellings

contract values before ADR-152 (capability `harbor`, source `harbor`, ids `harbor:<id>`, types harbor_bash / harbor_monitor, field harborPending): stored history and older servers / Runners still send them; read as the new values
a session from an older server still has the field by its old name (ADR-152)
the stop route's description: an id with the old prefix is still accepted (ADR-152)
tests that the contract values from before ADR-152 are still read as the new ones
Daisy's tools by their old names (MCP server `harbor`, the job field `harborTools`) for conversations started before ADR-154 and Runners from then
the refusal (its text now in the language packs, P6-23b) names the old tool prefix an older conversation knows (ADR-154); the old Runner state root stays denied (ADR-153)

entries.re: mcp__harbor__\w*|harbor_\w*|"harbor"|「harbor」|harborTools|HARBOR_NEEDS_FILES|Harbor (fork|rewind|系统|补送)|\(Harbor 注入|/Harbor/|/harbor/i|Harbor 定时与后台|这些由 Harbor 保存|你是 Harbor 的|你现在是 Harbor 的|the Harbor marker
entries.why: tests (and the fake agent) of the model-facing names from before ADR-154: old conversations keep their tool names, old marks and markers are still recognised, the old prompt snapshot is converted
the 「只问」 answer marker before ADR-154: a conversation asked then may still answer with it
the system sender's old name (「Harbor 系统」): stored items carry it (ADR-154); the reader's pattern takes it
a stored row from before the rename, under the old system sender (ADR-154)
copy markers written before ADR-154: a copy made then still carries one
redelivery prefixes before ADR-154: a job queued then still says so
worktrees and branches made under the old names are still found and used (ADR-153)
a Runner's old default state root, still used when it exists (ADR-153)
browser storage keys before ADR-153: moved to the new key on first read
the terminal page's handshake: a page or a window of an older Daisy says harbor-terminal-* (ADR-153)
the old system's database is recognised and refused with what to do, never imported or touched (D-06)
a comment inside schema step 1's SQL text, which is frozen: its hash is pinned (tests/schema-compat.test.ts V1_SHA256)
a private plugin's test driver: the provider name the external server matches changes together with that server
